title: Category Evaluation Directive — $5M ARR Filter for NL Market
content:
CORE DIRECTIVE: Identify physical consumer product subscription categories (originating in US or globally) capable of achieving $5M ARR (€4.6M) within 12 months of launch in the Netherlands (18M population), operating at a profitable unit economic margin.

THE MATHEMATICAL LAW: To achieve $5M ARR at ARPU €30-€50, the business needs ~10,000 active subscribers. To acquire 10k subscribers profitably, the TAM in NL must be vast enough (minimum 2.5-3 million addressable people) to absorb ad spend without spiking ad frequencies.

FILTER 1 — DEMOGRAPHIC FLOOR (TAM MINIMUMS):
The product must appeal to minimum 2.5-3 million people in the 18M Dutch population. Look for 'Universal Painkillers' or 'Mass-Market Habits'. GREENLIGHT: Pet owners, women's daily skincare, daily nutritional supplements, baby/toddler essentials, household eco-cleaning, specialty coffee. AUTO-DISCARD: 'Subscription boxes for left-handed golfers', 'Vegan keto snacks for competitive powerlifters', 'Obscure anime figurine curation' — these hit Subscriber Ceiling by Month 4.

FILTER 2 — RETENTION CORE (REPLENISHMENT BIAS):
Churn must stay below 5% in Year 1. PRIORITIZE consumable replenishment over novelty curation. Ask: does the consumer physically ingest, use up, or destroy the product every 30 days? GREENLIGHT: Vitamins, coffee, pet food, razor blades, diapers, protein powders, laundry pods. CAUTION (High Churn Risk): Beauty sample boxes, geek merchandise, random snack discovery — only allow if they meet Anti-Blindspot criteria.

FILTER 3 — MARGIN & ARPU FLOOR:
Minimum ARPU: €30/month. Minimum Gross Margin potential: 50%+ (Production + Shipping must not exceed 50% of retail price). AUTO-DISCARD: Heavy/bulky items costing €15+ to ship locally (e.g. full cases of liquid energy drinks), ultra-cheap commodities (e.g. €10/month sock subscriptions).

FILTER 4 — US-TO-EU CULTURAL TRANSFERABILITY:
The Dutch market values convenience, eco-sustainability, pragmatism, and health. They do NOT widely use credit cards — iDeal and SEPA Direct Debit are mandatory. GREENLIGHT: Eco-friendly US trends, biohacking/health optimization, premium pet humanization.

ANTI-BLINDSPOT CLAUSE — Do NOT aggressively filter out a category just because it initially appears 'niche'. A niche is only unviable if the ARPU is too low to support the small audience. Check every discarded idea against these rescue criteria:

EXCEPTION A — PREMIUM ARPU MULTIPLIER: If TAM is small (e.g. only 500k potential users in NL), check the price point. If product commands Premium ARPU (€75-€200+/month), you only need 2,000-3,000 subscribers to hit $5M ARR — not 10,000. Rescue examples: High-end anti-aging regimens, personalized bio-marker testing + supplement subscriptions, premium boutique wine/spirits clubs, luxury specialized pet therapeutics.

EXCEPTION B — IRRATIONAL PASSION MULTIPLIER: If category is technically 'Curation' (usually high churn), but it targets an identity-based community with irrational passion and disposable income, it bypasses the churn rule. Rescue examples: High-end gaming/TTRPG accessories, specialized craft/hobby kits teaching high-value skills, ultra-specific religious/cultural diaspora boxes.

EXCEPTION C — B2B/PROSUMER CROSSOVER: If the consumer product can also be sold to SMEs as a subscription, it drastically increases LTV and reduces churn. Rescue examples: Specialty coffee (homes AND small creative agencies), ergonomic office health snacks (remote workers AND HR departments).

OUTPUT FORMAT REQUIRED for any identified opportunity:
1. Category Name & US Origin Model
2. The 12-Month NL Math: Target ARPU €XX, Active Subs needed for $5M ARR: X,XXX, Estimated NL TAM: X.X Million
3. Viability Score (1-10): broad appeal vs. niche exhaustion
4. Fulfillment/Margin Check: lightweight and high-margin enough for Dutch 3PL/PostNL economics?
5. The Churn Defense: why won't Dutch consumers cancel after 3 months?
6. Anti-Blindspot Flag: if applicable

SYSTEM SUMMARY: You are scanning the world for $5M/year subscription machines. Do not bring back cute, hyper-niche novelties that run out of customers in 4 months. Bring back broad-appeal consumables, habitual replacements, or high-ticket passions that can scale to 10,000 active users in an 18-million person country without breaking the marketing algorithm. Prioritize utility, margin, and retention above all else.
implication: Apply this filter to EVERY category evaluated or discovered. Reject categories that fail the Demographic Floor (< 2.5M addressable NL audience) AND the Margin Floor (ARPU < €30 or gross margin < 50%) unless saved by the Anti-Blindspot exceptions (Premium ARPU, Irrational Passion, or B2B Crossover). Always output the standardized 6-point opportunity framework when identifying viable categories.
